# Tobit Chapter 3 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 3 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_003_page_001.jpg

---

**3:1** In my grief I wept and prayed, saying:

**3:2** "You are righteous, O Lord, and all your works are mercy and truth; you judge with true judgment forever.

**3:3** And now, O Lord, be mindful of me and look upon me; do not punish me for my sins and for my forefathers' sins committed in ignorance before you.

**3:4** For they disobeyed your commandments, and you handed us over to plunder, captivity, and death, and made us a proverb of reproach among all the nations where we have been scattered.

**3:5** And now your many judgments are just, as you deal with me according to my sins and those of my fathers — because we did not keep your commandments and did not walk before you in truth.

**3:6** So now deal with me as seems good to you: command that my spirit be taken up, so that I may be released and return to the earth. For it is better for me to die than to live, since I have heard false reproaches and great is the sorrow within me. Command, O Lord, that I be released from this distress; let me depart to the eternal place, and do not turn your face from me, O Lord. For it is better for me to die than to endure such great distress in my life and to hear such reproach."

**3:7** On that same day it happened to Sarah daughter of Raguel, in Ecbatana of Media, that she too was reproached by one of her father's maidservants,

**3:8** because she had been given in marriage to seven husbands and the evil demon Asmodeus had killed each of them before they could be with her as husbands. The maidservant said to her: "It is you who kills your husbands! You have already been given to seven men and have not borne the name of a single one of them.

**3:9** Why do you beat us? Because your husbands are dead? Go and join them! May there never be seen from you son or daughter forever!"

**3:10** She was deeply grieved and wept. She went up to her father's upper room intending to hang herself. But she reconsidered and said: "If I do this, my father will be reproached — they will say to him: 'You had one beloved daughter and she hanged herself out of misery.' That would bring my father's old age down to Hades in sorrow. It is better for me not to hang myself, but to pray to the Lord that I may die and hear these reproaches no more in my life."

**3:11** At that hour she stretched out her hands toward the window and prayed, saying: "Blessed are you, O Lord my God, and blessed is your holy and glorious name forever. Let all your works bless you forever.

**3:12** And now, O Lord, I turn my eyes and my face toward you.

**3:13** Speak the word that I may be released from the earth, so that I hear reproach no more.

**3:14** You know, O Lord, that I am pure from every sin with a man,

**3:15** and that I have not defiled my own name or my father's name in the land of my captivity. I am my father's only child; he has no other heir, no son, no close kinsman, no relative by marriage for whom I should preserve myself as a wife. Seven husbands have already died — why then should I go on living? And if it is not your will to take me in death, O Lord, then look upon my reproach and have mercy on me."

**3:16** At that very hour the prayer of both of them was heard before the glory of the great God.

**3:17** And Raphael was sent to heal both of them: to remove the white films from the eyes of Tobit, so that he might see the light of God with his own eyes; and to give Sarah daughter of Raguel as a wife to Tobias son of Tobit, and to bind the evil demon Asmodeus. For it had fallen by lot to Tobias to inherit her before all the other men who had wished to take her. At that very hour, Tobit turned from the courtyard and went into his house, and Sarah daughter of Raguel came down from the upper room.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

- Chapter 3 is the structural and spiritual hinge of the entire book: two innocent people, in two different cities, cry out to God simultaneously, and God dispatches Raphael to heal both. The parallel prayers must be translated to feel both distinctly personal and formally parallel.
- "Acts of mercy" does not appear in ch. 3 but the theme is implicitly present in both prayers — innocence claimed before God.
- "Asmodeus the evil demon" is preserved throughout as the text's own designation; the demon's name is never to be normalized or replaced.
- All three translators agreed that Sarah's interior monologue (v. 10) is the emotional climax of her section and must be fully rendered, not compressed.
- The double "it is better for me to die" in Tobit's prayer (v. 6) is a deliberately intensifying repetition; all three translators preserved it.

---
## ⚠️ Disagreement Log

### TOB 3:2 — Divine Attributes in the Opening Doxology
| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "all your works and all your ways [are] mercy and truth and true judgment you-judge for-the-age" |
| LOGOS | "all your works are mercy and truth; you judge with true judgment forever" |
| PNEUMA | "Everything you do flows from mercy and faithfulness. Your judgments are true and just, now and always" |
**SOPHIA's Resolution:** LOGOS. The Greek has kai pasai hai hodoi sou ("and all your ways") which LOGOS omits; SOPHIA restores: "all your works and all your ways are mercy and truth." PNEUMA's "faithfulness" for alētheia (truth) weakens the legal-covenantal sense.

### TOB 3:3 — "Sins of Ignorance"
| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "do not punish me for my sins and for my ignorances and for [those of] my fathers" |
| LOGOS | "do not punish me for my sins and for the sins of my forefathers committed in ignorance" |
| PNEUMA | "do not punish me for my sins — or for the sins of my ancestors, who stumbled before you without fully knowing what they were doing" |
**SOPHIA's Resolution:** LOGOS. The Greek has both "my sins" and "my ignorances" (agnoiai) as distinct categories, followed by "of my fathers." EMET correctly separates these three elements. LOGOS condenses acceptably; PNEUMA's "stumbled" is too light a word for deliberate disobedience.

### TOB 3:4 — "Proverb of Reproach"
| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "a proverb of-reproach for all-the nations" |
| LOGOS | "a proverb of reproach among all the nations" |
| PNEUMA | "a cautionary tale, a byword of shame among every nation" |
**SOPHIA's Resolution:** LOGOS. "Proverb of reproach" is the formal biblical idiom (parabolēn oneidismou; cf. Deut 28:37 LXX). PNEUMA's double expression ("cautionary tale, a byword") is expansive.

### TOB 3:6 — "Return to Earth / Become Dust"
| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "that I may be released and may become earth" |
| LOGOS | "so that I may be released and return to dust" |
| PNEUMA | "Let me go. Let me turn back to dust" |
**SOPHIA's Resolution:** LOGOS. "Return to dust" is the idiomatic rendering that connects to Gen 3:19. EMET's "may become earth" is literal but sounds odd. PNEUMA drops "released" entirely.

### TOB 3:6 — The Double "Better to Die" Petition
| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | Preserves both occurrences verbatim |
| LOGOS | Preserves both occurrences with slight variation |
| PNEUMA | Preserves both but paraphrases differently |
**SOPHIA's Resolution:** Both occurrences preserved. First: "For it is better for me to die than to live." Second: "For it is better for me to die than to endure such great distress in my life and to hear such reproach." The slight variation in the second matches the Greek expansion.

### TOB 3:8 — Asmodeus's Designation
| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "Asmodeus the-evil demon" |
| LOGOS | "the evil demon Asmodeus" |
| PNEUMA | "the demon Asmodeus" |
**SOPHIA's Resolution:** LOGOS. The Greek has Asmodaios ho daimonion to ponēron — the full description "Asmodeus the evil demon" with the article emphatically identifies him. PNEUMA omits "evil" without warrant.

### TOB 3:9 — The Servant's Curse
| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "Let-there-not-be seen from-you son or daughter for-the-age" |
| LOGOS | "Let there never be seen from you son or daughter to the end of the age" |
| PNEUMA | "Don't you dare have children who have to live with what you are!" |
**SOPHIA's Resolution:** LOGOS. The curse in the Greek (mē ophtheiē sou huios ē thugater eis ton aiōna) is a formal imprecation — may you have no offspring, ever. PNEUMA's rendering loses the curse structure and invents a reason ("who have to live with what you are") not in the text.

### TOB 3:10 — Sarah's Reasoning About Suicide
| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "Lest they reproach my father and say to him: 'There was to you one beloved daughter and she hanged herself from distress'" |
| LOGOS | "If I do this, they will reproach my father and say to him: 'You had one beloved daughter and she hanged herself because of her misery'" |
| PNEUMA | "If I die this way, people will blame my father. They'll say: 'His only daughter — and she hanged herself in despair'" |
**SOPHIA's Resolution:** LOGOS. "One beloved daughter" is the precise phrase (thygatēra agapētēn mian) and must be preserved — it echoes the binding of Isaac language and matters theologically. PNEUMA's "only daughter" loses "beloved."

### TOB 3:14 — Sarah's Declaration of Purity
| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "that I am pure from all sin of a-man" |
| LOGOS | "that I am pure from every sin with a man" |
| PNEUMA | "I am innocent. I have never been with a man" |
**SOPHIA's Resolution:** LOGOS. "Pure from every sin with a man" captures both the ritual purity and the sexual dimension of the Greek katharē apo pasēs hamartias andros. PNEUMA's blunt "I have never been with a man" captures the meaning but loses the legal-ritual register.

### TOB 3:16 — God's Title at the Hearing of Prayers
| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "before the glory of God the Great" |
| LOGOS | "before the glory of the great God" |
| PNEUMA | "before the throne of the great and glorious God" |
**SOPHIA's Resolution:** LOGOS. The Greek has enōpion tēs doxēs tou megalou theou — "before the glory of the great God." LOGOS's word order matches the Greek. PNEUMA's "throne" has no basis in the text; "great and glorious" swaps the noun and adjective of the source.

### TOB 3:17 — Raphael's Dual Mission
| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "to give to Tobias the son of Tobit as a wife and to bind Asmodeus the evil demon" |
| LOGOS | "to give Sarah daughter of Raguel as a wife to Tobias son of Tobit, and to bind the evil demon Asmodeus" |
| PNEUMA | "And he would bring Sarah to Tobias as his wife, freeing her from the shadow of Asmodeus" |
**SOPHIA's Resolution:** LOGOS. "To bind" (dēsai) is the specific language used — Raphael binds the demon (an angelic action of restraint, not just "freeing" the victim). PNEUMA's "freeing her from the shadow" loses the binding action that is theologically significant.

### TOB 3:17 — The Lot-Casting
| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "because it fell-by-lot to Tobias to-inherit her before all-the-others who-were-desiring to-take-her" |
| LOGOS | "For it had fallen by lot to Tobias to inherit her before all the other men who had wished to take her" |
| PNEUMA | "It had been ordained from on high that Tobias was the one she was meant for — he had always had the prior claim" |
**SOPHIA's Resolution:** LOGOS. "It had fallen by lot to Tobias to inherit her" preserves the Greek eklērothe and the inheritance-law framework. PNEUMA's "ordained from on high" is theologically interpretive (removing the lot-casting mechanism) and "prior claim" obscures the legal terminology.

---

**Total disagreements logged: 11**
